pages.intro: `MfxClient` signs every request with your private key, applies a retry budget to reads, and opens the stream. Its namespaces - `client.terminals`, `client.execution` and the rest - are the other pages. `SyncMfxClient` is the same surface for code with no event loop. Secrets and signing keys render as `***` in every repr, log line and traceback.

types.doc: An operation is over in any of these; every other state is on its way (TerminalOperation).

types.doc: The states a terminal passes through on its way to ACTIVE; every other state is settled.

types.name: Id
types.doc: Ids are uuids on the wire and in the generated models. Callers may hand over either, because a tenant reading an id out of its own database has a string and should not have to know that.

types.name: OFFLINE_IS_TEMPORARY
types.doc: OFFLINE needs nothing from you. The platform brings the terminal back by itself when its host reports again, and moves it to another host of its farm when the host's VM is gone or the host is still down after fifteen minutes. Retrying a request against an OFFLINE terminal is the right thing to do; re-creating the terminal is not.

types.name: is_usable
types.doc:
Can this terminal be used right now — market data, execution, account reads?

True only in ACTIVE. Every other state means not yet (REQUESTED, PROVISIONING, LOGGING_IN), not any more (DRAINING, RETIRED), not until it is resumed (DRAINED), or not at the moment (OFFLINE, FAILED). QUEUED is not yet: the terminal is placed and waits for its turn to start, because its host starts terminals a few at a time. `terminal.queue` says its place, its expected start and why it waits; [Terminals.wait_until_active](#terminals.Terminals.wait_until_active) waits on it.

`OFFLINE` is the state worth knowing about, because it is the one that used to be hidden inside ACTIVE: the terminal is fine, its *host* is not — turned off outside MFX Hub, its VM missing in Azure, or silent for three minutes. `terminal.offline_reason` says which of the three. It is not something to act on: see [OFFLINE_IS_TEMPORARY](#terminals.OFFLINE_IS_TEMPORARY).

members.name: create
members.signature: async def create(*, broker_id: Id, server_id: Id, idempotency_key: str, farm_id: Id | None = None, streaming: bool = False, execution: bool = False, instruments: list[str] | None = None, labels: dict[str, str] | None = None, redundancy: Redundancy = 'none') -> TenantTerminal
members.doc:
Ask for a terminal. Answered at once in state `REQUESTED`.

The move to a host is asynchronous, and the credential is submitted separately, so a terminal exists before its login does. `instruments` are the broker's own symbol names (`EURUSD.sd`): MFX never renames an instrument on a tenant's behalf.

**`farm_id` is optional**. Leave it out and the platform chooses: your own ACTIVE farms first, then the shared ones, offering the usages this terminal needs, in the server's region, with room; the oldest wins a tie. The farm it picked is on the answer, so the choice is never silent. Naming one is still the way to place a terminal deliberately, and it is checked rather than trusted: a farm that is not yours, or cannot take it, is refused.

members.doc:
Restart a stuck terminal: the terminal is closed and started again on the same host.

Answered `202` with the operation to follow; the terminal is not back until the operation succeeds, which takes a minute or two. `reason` is required and is **shown to operators in the console's activity feed and read back by this API**, so it is written for a person, not for a tracker.

`confirm_open_positions` has no default on purpose at the platform: a restart drops the broker session for a few seconds, and on an account with positions open that is a decision the caller makes deliberately. Positions live at the broker and are not closed by a restart; the flag is there so nobody does this to a live account without saying so.

Seven rules govern it: a cooldown, a rate limit, one operation at a time per terminal, and the states a restart can act on. A refusal names its rule in `error.code`, with `Retry-After` when waiting is what helps.

`queue` is true unless given. A valid restart refused only because the platform is busy is then answered `202` with the operation `QUEUED`, and it starts on its own when its turn comes. `queue=False` keeps the refusal instead, as a 409 or 429 with `Retry-After`, for a caller that would rather decide when to try again.

members.doc:
Keep the position's stop loss `distance` behind the best price it reaches.

`distance` is a price difference above zero - `Decimal("0.0020")` on EURUSD is twenty pips - and a `float` is refused. The platform moves the broker's stop, only ever tighter, at most once a second and by at least a tenth of the distance. Setting again replaces the distance and keeps what the stop has reached. A stop loss set by anyone else ends it, and the stream says so (`position.trailing_stop_changed`). Refused as a result with `invalid_stops` when the distance is inside the symbol's stops level, and `invalid_request` when the ticket is not an open position of the account.

types.name: Reason
types.doc:
Why a command ended as it did.

The platform's dictionary of reasons plus the four the SDK itself can conclude. A reason the platform adds later arrives as its own string rather than as one of these — see [ExecutionResult.reason_text](#execution.ExecutionResult.reason_text) — because bucketing a reason the caller has never seen is how a granular vocabulary quietly becomes "failed".

members.name: MAINTENANCE
members.doc: A planned maintenance window suspended order placement for this terminal: the API refused it with 403 `maintenance`, or a command queued before the window was refused by the platform before it ran. Nothing reached the broker, so it is **retryable** once the window ends - [ExecutionResult.retry_at](#execution.ExecutionResult.retry_at) says when, where the platform said.

members.name: VENUE_UNAVAILABLE
members.doc: The venue did not answer, or its connection to the account is down: nothing was placed, and the platform marks it **retryable**.

members.name: NOT_ON_THIS_VENUE
members.doc: The account's venue has no equivalent for what was asked (on cTrader: a stop-limit whose limit is on the better side of its stop, or a trailing stop). Not retryable as it stands.

members.name: TRANSPORT_ERROR
members.doc: Concluded by the SDK, never sent by the platform: the request never got an answer.

members.name: TIMEOUT
members.doc: Concluded by the SDK: no answer in time. **Never retried** — a timed-out order may have been placed, and deal-history reconciliation is the only safe recovery.

members.name: REFUSED
members.doc: The platform refused the request itself: a 4xx that is not a rate limit.

types.name: CommandState
types.doc: Final: SUCCEEDED, FAILED, EXPIRED, REJECTED. UNKNOWN is visible and not final.

types.name: Tickets
types.doc: The terminal relates one order, one deal and one position per fill; null where it has none yet.

types.name: VenueDeal
types.doc: One deal a command made, as the venue reported it (cTrader): two for an emulated close-by, one for an order filled at once. `volume_units` is in units of the instrument, not lots.

types.name: ExecutionResult
types.doc:
The whole answer to one execution call. Never raised — always returned.

Read `state` first: `SUCCEEDED` is done; `FAILED`, `EXPIRED` and `REJECTED` did not happen; `UNKNOWN` may already be a position and must never be sent again under a new key. `final` says whether the platform can still change the answer; [Execution.wait_for](#execution.Execution.wait_for) waits until it cannot.

types.name: SubscriptionDegraded
types.doc:
A subscription whose symbol cannot tick, or should be ticking and is not.

Sent once, when it becomes degraded. A closed market is not a degradation, and neither is a terminal that restarts and is back inside a few minutes. `reason` is the platform's own word and is text, not a closed list: `symbol_removed`, `subscription_refused`, `terminal_disconnected`, `report_stale` and `no_ticks_in_session` today, and a platform that learns another will send it. A reason that gives way to another while the subscription stays degraded sends nothing; read the subscription for the one that holds.

types.name: SubscriptionRecovered
types.doc:
A degraded subscription that is delivering again. Sent once.

`reason` is what it recovered from and `since` when it had become degraded, so the two together with `recovered_at` are the whole gap, without the first message being kept.

types.name: Book
types.doc:
A symbol's whole order book as one terminal read it. Replace yours with every one.

Prices and volumes are `Decimal`, exact as the platform sent them. `levels` is the most a side the platform reads, so a side shorter than it is the broker's whole side. Not a reconstruction: MFX Hub builds no book from ticks or from several terminals.

members.name: best_bid
members.doc: The highest buy price, or None when the book has no bids.

members.name: best_ask
members.doc: The lowest sell price, or None when the book has no asks.

types.name: book_of
types.doc:
A message from a `book:` channel as the [Book](#market-data.Book) it is, or None for any other.

.. code-block:: python

```
await stream.subscribe(Channel.book(server_id, "XAUUSD"))
async for message in stream:
    book = book_of(message)
    if book is not None:
        spread = book.best_ask - book.best_bid
```

The first message after a subscribe is the newest book the platform holds; each later one is a change. A gap in `seq` is a book superseded before it reached you, not a lost fact.

types.name: subscription_event
types.signature: def subscription_event(message: StreamMessage) -> SubscriptionDegraded | SubscriptionRecovered | None
types.doc:
A message from `events` as the subscription-health event it is, or None for any other.

.. code-block:: python

```
async for message in stream:
    health = subscription_event(message)
    if isinstance(health, SubscriptionDegraded):
        pause(health.symbol, why=health.reason)
```

A subscription keeps its stream while it is degraded: nothing needs subscribing again when it recovers. The same two facts are on the subscription itself (`state`, `degraded_reason`, `degraded_since`) for a caller that was not listening.

A symbol's bars for a window, oldest first: at most 1,000 a call.

The bars are the ones the broker's server shows the tenant's own account, read through one of its ACTIVE terminals on that server. When the window holds more than `limit` bars the answer is the **newest** of them, so a chart asking for "up to now" gets the bars nearest now; ask again with an earlier `to` for the ones before. The bar still forming is included when the window reaches it: its close is the last price.

`timeframe` is one of M1, M5, M15, M30, H1, H4, D1, W1, MN1; any other is a `ValueError` here, before the wire. Each bar's `ts` is its open time as a true instant: a daily bar opens at the broker's midnight, which is not UTC midnight. `symbol` is the broker's own name. With terminals on more than one of the broker's servers, name `server_id`. No bar in the window is an empty answer, not an error.

A cTrader account's bars for a window, oldest first: at most 1,000 a call.

The cTrader counterpart of [candles](#market-data.MarketData.candles), keyed on the account instead of a broker and server. The bars are Spotware's trendbars for the account's own symbol name, in UTC, `v` the bar's tick volume. When the window holds more than `limit` bars the answer is the **newest** of them; the bar still forming is included when the window reaches now. Nothing is stored: the account's runner reads them, and each read counts against the same per-terminal limit a minute as [candles](#market-data.MarketData.candles) (a 429 is retried with the platform's `Retry-After`, and raised as [RateLimitError](#errors.RateLimitError) once it runs out).

A MetaTrader 5 account is a [StateError](#errors.StateError) (`details["reason"] == "not_on_this_venue"`): its candles are its server's, so use [candles](#market-data.MarketData.candles). An account whose runner is not connected is an [UpstreamError](#errors.UpstreamError) (503). No bar in the window is an empty answer.

members.signature: async def all_ticks(broker: Id, symbol: str, *, from_: dt.datetime, to: dt.datetime | None = None, page_size: int | None = None, server_id: Id | None = None) -> AsyncIterator[Tick]
members.doc:
Every tick of a window, in order, each once, a call at a time.

The contract's way to continue is to ask again from the last tick's time, and several ticks can share one millisecond, so the next answer begins with ticks already held. This drops exactly those and yields the rest, which is easy to get subtly wrong by hand: drop by time alone and ticks are lost, drop nothing and they are doubled.

Every call is a round trip to a host (a busy symbol passes 100,000 ticks a day): this is for reading history. The stream is the way to follow ticks as they happen.

types.name: StreamClosed
types.doc: The connection ended. `code` is the WebSocket close code, `reason` the server's words.

types.name: StreamConnection
types.doc:
What this module needs of a WebSocket, and nothing more.

Narrow on purpose: it keeps the library choice out of every other module, and it lets the reconnect and gap logic — the part that is easy to get wrong — be tested against a socket that closes exactly when the test says to.

members.name: recv
members.doc: The next frame, or raise [StreamClosed](#stream.StreamClosed) when the connection has ended.

types.name: StreamMessage
types.doc: One message on one channel.

types.name: Resync
types.doc:
The requested position is older than the replay window: read current state over REST.

Delivered rather than raised, because it is not an error — it is the platform being honest that it cannot replay this far back, and the remedy is a read, not a retry.

types.name: ChannelRefused
types.doc:
The platform refused one channel. Every other channel on this stream is unaffected.

Delivered rather than raised. A refusal is about one channel, and raising it out of `async for message in stream` ended the whole connection: a tenant following hundreds of terminals lost every one of them because a single terminal had been retired since it last subscribed. That is the common case, not an exotic one - `not_found` is exactly what the platform answers for a terminal that is gone, or was never this tenant's.

The subscription is dropped when this arrives, so a reconnect does not ask for it again and collect the same refusal for the life of the process. A caller that believes the channel should exist subscribes again and finds out again.

An error that names no channel is about the connection itself and is still raised.

members.name: account

One terminal's live account: a snapshot, then marks.

Account *state* has its own channel per terminal rather than riding `events`, because state is latest-wins and events may not be lost: at thousands of terminals, snapshots competing with fills for one 15-minute replay window turns that window over in seconds. Use [LiveAccount](#stream.LiveAccount) to merge what arrives; `position.opened`/`closed` still arrive on `events`, which is where notifications and history belong.

members.doc: The symbol's order book as one of the tenant's terminals reads it: an `md.book` message with the whole book each time it changes; read it with [book_of](#market-data.book_of). Granted as [md](#stream.Channel.md) is - `md:read` and a live subscription to the symbol - and it carries nothing until a terminal on that server reads the symbol's depth (`depth_instruments`, [Terminals.replace_instruments](#terminals.Terminals.replace_instruments)).

members.name: stats
members.doc: What has been missed so far. A snapshot; it never mutates under the caller.

members.name: channels
members.doc: The channels currently subscribed, in the order they were asked for.

members.name: subscribe
members.doc:
Subscribe to one channel. The platform acknowledges it on the stream.

Subscribing twice is not an error: the channel is already being watched, and a caller re-asserting its subscriptions after its own restart should not have to remember.

members.name: resume
members.doc:
Ask the platform to bring one channel back up to date, from the last seq seen.

The SDK does this for you across a reconnect. This is for the other case: the caller has noticed, from the data itself, that its own view is behind — which only it can know. On `account:{terminal_id}` that is the documented remedy for a `seq` gap or an unapplicable marks message (the stream's resume rule), and the answer there is a fresh snapshot rather than a replay.

On a channel that does not replay, and on one never subscribed, this subscribes instead of resuming. Both are the honest request: there is no position to resume from, so asking to carry on from one would be asking for something the platform cannot give, and a caller would be left with a silent channel rather than a current one.

members.name: unsubscribe
members.doc: Stop watching a channel, and stop resubscribing to it after a reconnect.

members.name: aclose
members.doc:
Close the stream for good, if it is open. `async with` does this for you.

A read that is waiting ends with nothing, and a reconnect under way is given up: closing is the caller's decision, not a drop to recover from.

types.doc: `order.closed`: a pending order left the account. On `filled`, `position_ticket` is the position it became (also on that position's `order_ticket`).

types.name: PositionOpened
types.doc: `position.opened`: a position appeared on the account.

types.name: PositionModified
types.doc: `position.modified`: a position's stops or volume changed.

types.name: PositionClosed
types.doc: `position.closed`: a position left the account.

types.doc: `terminal.state_changed`: a terminal moved from one state to another.

types.name: event_of

A stream message as the typed event it is, or None for a message of any other type.

A candle is read by its channel: `candles:` messages carry the bar and no event type. A message of one of these types that lacks a field the contract requires is a ValueError naming the field.

types.name: AccountView
types.doc:
One terminal's account as the stream last said it was: a snapshot, with the marks applied.

`positions` is keyed by ticket because that is how a mark names the position it moves, and because a caller drawing a table wants to find a row rather than scan for it. The order is the snapshot's own - dicts keep insertion order - so rendering it twice reads the same way.

types.name: LiveAccount
types.doc:
The stream's ordering rules, applied to the events you hand it.

Not a subscriber: it holds no socket and asks for nothing. The caller drives the stream, which is what lets one connection follow several terminals and lets a caller who already has an event loop keep it.

params.name: terminal_id
params.doc: The terminal whose account this view follows.

members.name: view
members.doc:
The account, or `None` until the first snapshot arrives.

`None` rather than an empty view: an account with no positions and a zero balance is a statement about a tenant's money, and "we have not been told yet" is not that statement.

members.name: behind
members.doc:
True when a message could not be applied, so this view is not the account.

The remedy is `resume`, which answers with a snapshot. Waiting is also correct - a snapshot comes within 60 s by itself - but until one does, do not show these figures as live.

members.name: apply
members.doc:
Take one stream event. Returns the new view, or `None` if nothing was applied.

`None` deliberately covers several things, because a caller does the same for all of them - draw nothing new, then check [behind](#stream.LiveAccount.behind): an event for another channel, terminal or kind; a marks message that does not apply; a resync; and a sequence gap.

pages.intro: What a read or a write outside execution can raise, mapped from the API's error code. Execution methods never raise; they return a result.

types.name: MfxError
types.doc: Every failure this SDK raises.

types.name: MfxTransportError
types.doc:
The request never got an answer: DNS, TCP, TLS, a dropped connection.

`may_have_reached` says whether the request could have arrived. It is False only when the connection never opened, so nothing was sent; a connection that dropped after the request was written may have delivered it, and an order sent that way may already be a position.

types.name: MfxTimeout
types.doc: The request got no answer in time. Never retried by the SDK for a write.

types.name: MfxApiError
types.doc: MFX answered, and the answer was a failure.

types.name: ValidationError
types.doc: The request was refused before anything happened: 400, or 422 for an unsupported broker.

types.name: AuthError
types.doc: The signature, key, timestamp or nonce was not accepted.

types.name: ForbiddenError
types.doc: The key is valid and this is not in its scopes.

types.name: TenantDisabledError
types.doc:
The operator has disabled this tenant: every call is refused until it is enabled.

Nothing is wrong with the key, its scopes or the request, and retrying changes nothing: it ends when the operator enables the tenant. `message` is what the operator wrote for the tenant, word for word, and is the thing to show or log. The tenant's terminals keep running meanwhile. An open stream is closed with the same error.

members.name: since
members.doc: When the tenant was disabled; None if the platform did not say.

types.name: TenantSuspendedError
types.doc:
The operator has suspended this tenant: writes are refused now, reads for a while yet.

Orders, closes and every other write are refused from the moment of suspension. Reads and the stream go on working until `reads_until`, the end of the suspension's grace, and are then refused with this same error. It is not retryable: it ends when the operator resumes the tenant. `message` is what the operator wrote for the tenant, word for word.

Execution methods never raise: a suspended tenant's order comes back as a refused `ExecutionResult` whose `detail` carries this error's text.

members.name: since
members.doc: When the suspension began; None if the platform did not say.

members.name: reads_until
members.doc: When reads stop working too; None if the platform named no grace.

types.name: MaintenanceError
types.doc:
A planned maintenance window suspends this for you until [ends_at](#errors.MaintenanceError.ends_at).

403 `maintenance`. Nothing is wrong with the key or the request: it works again when the window ends, so wait until `ends_at` and send it again (the same idempotency key for a write). Only the window's own scope is refused, and open positions are never closed by a window. `message` is the platform's sentence ("Paused for planned maintenance until 02:38 UTC.") and is the part to show a person; `client.maintenance.list()` says what else is suspended and is answered throughout.

members.name: window
members.doc: The window's label as people say it: `MW-0031`.

members.name: ends_at
members.doc: The window's current end, aware; None if the platform did not say. It can move.

members.name: service
members.doc: The suspended service that refused this call, e.g. `order_placement`.

members.name: suspended
members.doc: Every service the window suspends for you.

types.name: RiskRefusal
types.doc: What a Risk Management refusal names: the rule, the figures and the policy or challenge behind it, as a refusal's details and a copy refusal's `risk` carry them. Figures stay text, as the platform wrote them; `policy_id` and `version` are None when a challenge's rule refused, and `challenge_id` and `challenge_version` are None when a policy's did.

types.name: RiskRefusedError
types.doc: 422 `risk_refused`: a new entry broke a Risk Management rule in force on the account and nothing was sent to the broker. `refusal` says which rule, the figure it used, its limit and what the entry would have made it. Send a smaller entry, add a stop, or wait for the inputs to be fresh (`reason` `risk_inputs_stale`) or for the window to open.

members.name: refusal
members.doc: What refused the entry, read from `details`.

types.name: RiskOverrideRequiredError
types.doc: 403 `risk_override_required`: the change relaxes protection, and needs a key with `risk:override` and a `reason`. Nothing was changed.

types.name: PaymentRequiredError
types.doc:
402: a payment is missing. Not retryable unchanged: it ends when someone pays.

[BillingPaymentRequiredError](#errors.BillingPaymentRequiredError) is the one the platform sends with an API key; a 402 whose code this version does not know arrives as this class, by its status.

types.name: BillingAction
types.doc:
What clears a billing standing (the contract's `BillingAction`).

`kind` is `top_up` or `pay_invoice`. `portal_path` is the portal page that does it, relative to the portal's address (`/billing/top-up`): join it to the portal's address to give a person a link. `amount_usd` is at least what clears it, exact; `invoice_id` is the invoice to pay, None for a top-up.

types.name: BillingPaymentRequiredError
types.doc:
402 `billing_payment_required`: a payment is missing on the billing profile the request falls under, and nothing was done.

It is **not retryable**: sending the same request again changes nothing until the payment is made. At `stage` `reminder` it comes only from a request that adds something billed (a new account, an add-on switched on). Once `stage` is `suspended` it can come from **any write** on the tenant or the profile - orders, account changes, copy settings - whatever route it was sent to, not only the routes that document it. **Reads keep working** throughout, the billing reads (`client.billing`) included.

What a caller does: show `message` and [action](#errors.BillingPaymentRequiredError.action) to a person. `action.portal_path` is the portal page where they fix it (a top-up, or the invoice to pay), relative to the portal's address. Once paid, the accounts are released, usually within the hour; then send the request again (a write under the same idempotency key). `pay_by` is the last moment a payment avoids the suspension that begins at `suspends_at`.

Execution methods never raise: an order refused for billing comes back as a refused `ExecutionResult` whose `detail` carries this error's text.

members.name: billing_profile_id
members.doc: The billing profile the request falls under; on Standard, its one profile.

members.name: stage
members.doc: `reminder` (only what adds something billed is refused) or `suspended` (every write on the profile's accounts is). Read a word you do not know as text.

members.name: since
members.doc: When the stage began, aware; None if the platform did not say.

members.name: suspends_at
members.doc: The first suspended moment, aware; None if the platform did not say.

members.name: pay_by
members.doc: The last moment a payment avoids the suspension, aware; None if not said.

members.name: action
members.doc: What clears it, with the portal page that does it; None if the platform named none.

types.name: NotFoundError
types.doc: No such object *for this tenant*. Another tenant's id is a 404 here, never a 403.

types.name: ConflictError
types.doc: The request cannot apply to the object as it is now.

types.name: StateError
types.doc: The object is in a state this cannot be done from.

types.name: PlacementError
types.doc: No farm can carry what was asked for.

types.name: UnsupportedBrokerError
types.doc:
MFX does not support this broker or this server *now*.

Refused at request time and never passed to a terminal, so a tenant learns it here rather than from a terminal that sits in `REQUESTED` and never moves. `message` is the sentence an operator recorded, which is the part worth showing a user; the rest says which of the two switches was closed:

- `refused_by` — `permission` (the broker's legal position: MFX may not carry it for this tenant) or `server_disabled` (the broker is fine, this one server is switched off).
- `reason`, `broker_id`, `server_id` — as the platform recorded them.

The distinction matters to a caller: `server_disabled` means try another server of the same broker, `permission` means this broker is not available at all.

members.name: refused_by
members.doc: `permission` or `server_disabled`; None if the platform did not say.

members.name: reason
members.doc: The platform's own reason code, unbucketed.

members.name: broker_id
members.doc: The broker the refusal concerns, when the platform names one.

members.name: server_id
members.doc: The broker server the refusal concerns, when the platform names one.

types.name: DocumentDue
types.doc:
A legal document version the organisation must accept before it can add anything.

`document` is the document's key: `terms`, `mt5_licence`, or a plan's Service Agreement, `service_agreement_<plan>` (`service_agreement_enterprise`). The list is open: read a key you do not know as one more document, by its name. `number` is the version, `plan` the plan an agreement belongs to (None for the Terms and the licence), and `grace_ends_at` when its grace period ends or ended, aware; None for a plan change's agreement, which waits for acceptance instead.

types.name: PlanChange
types.doc:
A move from one plan to another, as the customer sees it (the contract's `PlanChangeSummary`).

`from_` is the plan in force and `to` the plan after acceptance; `state` is `awaiting_acceptance`, `active`, `lapsed` or `withdrawn` (read a word you do not know as text). `until` is when an awaiting change lapses if nobody accepts it, None once decided. `requested_by_operator` is True when MFX Hub asked for the change, False when the organisation did, None if the platform did not say.

types.name: TermsNotAccepted
types.doc:
409 `terms_not_accepted`: a Terms of Service or MetaTrader 5 licence version the organisation must accept is past its grace period unaccepted, and nothing was done.

Only additions are refused - a new terminal, attaching an expert advisor. Nothing running is touched: reads, orders, positions, restarts and detaches all work. It is **not retryable** unchanged: an owner or admin of the organisation accepts the version in the customer portal, then send the request again (a write under the same idempotency key). [documents](#errors.TermsNotAccepted.documents) names each version due.

members.name: documents
members.doc: Each document version due, with when its grace period ended.

types.name: ServiceAgreementNotAccepted
types.doc:
409 `service_agreement_not_accepted`: a plan change awaits acceptance of the new plan's Service Agreement, or a version of the plan's agreement is past its grace period unaccepted, and nothing was done.

Only additions are refused - a new terminal, attaching an expert advisor, generating or replacing an API key, asking for higher limits. Nothing running is touched: reads, orders, positions and anything already running all work. While a plan change waits, the plan in force stays as it is. Where the Terms are held as well, this is the error that answers, and [documents](#errors.ServiceAgreementNotAccepted.documents) lists every document due.

It is **not retryable** unchanged. What a caller does: show `message` and [accept_url](#errors.ServiceAgreementNotAccepted.accept_url) to a person; an owner or admin of the organisation accepts there, then send the request again (a write under the same idempotency key). `client.tenant.service_agreement()` says what is due at any time.

members.name: plan_change
members.doc: The plan change awaiting acceptance; None when there is none or it cannot be read.

members.name: documents
members.doc: Each document version due: the new plan's agreement, and any other held with it.

members.name: accept_url
members.doc: Where an owner or admin accepts, in the customer portal; None if not said.

types.name: RateLimitError
types.doc: The key is over its budget. `retry_after_s` is the server's own answer.

types.name: UpstreamError
types.doc:
Something MFX depends on did not answer as it needs: your terminal, the broker, or a service of its own. Always 503 from the platform, told apart by `error.code`:

- `upstream_error` - your terminal or the broker, raised as this class: `reason` says why where there is one (`terminal_timeout`, `deals_unreadable`, `no_tick` ...). No `Retry-After`: whether waiting helps depends on the terminal, so read its state first.
- `dependency_unavailable` - a store of the platform's own, raised as [DependencyUnavailableError](#errors.DependencyUnavailableError); `retry_after_s` says when.

The platform never answers 502 or 504. One of those came from the network in between (the edge's own page, with no MFX body), and is raised as [EdgeError](#errors.EdgeError), `from_edge` true. Both are subclasses, so `except UpstreamError` still catches all three.

members.name: reason
members.doc: The platform's word for what failed (`details.reason`), or None when it gave none.

members.name: from_edge
members.doc: True for a 502 or 504: not the platform's answer, the network's.

types.name: DependencyUnavailableError
types.doc:
503 `dependency_unavailable`: a store of the platform's own did not answer.

Not your terminal and not the broker: the request was valid, and waiting `retry_after_s` and sending it again is the right thing to do.

types.name: EdgeError
types.doc:
A 502 or 504 with no MFX body: the network in front of MFX Hub answered, not the platform.

MFX Hub never answers either itself, so this says the platform could not be reached, not that it failed. A write may or may not have arrived: retry it with the same idempotency key, which answers the original if it did.

types.name: InternalError
types.doc: MFX failed, and it is not the caller's request that is wrong.
